The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the approved 1962 Benziger printing sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.

No comma before the trailing Deus, with DO and with the approved Benziger printing, which sets Spíritus Sancti Deus without a break: Deus is in apposition to the subject Qui, and a comma here would read as though a new address began. The page points the Son's title differently, with commas after Christus (w031) and tuus (w033), which the edition keeps.
